title: 📘 UNIT 2: CLIMATE OF AFRICA
notes:
🌦️ Climate → the average of weather conditions in a place over a long period, usually 30 years or more.

☁️ Weather → the short-term condition of the atmosphere, such as temperature, precipitation, humidity, cloudiness and wind.

🌍 Climatic zone → a broad area with similar climatic conditions.

📍 Climatic region → a continuous geographic area with similar climate characteristics.

☀️ Earth's climate is mainly driven by solar energy received as radiation.

⭐ Africa's climate is mainly warm and tropical, with rainfall varying more than temperature.

🌍 Africa has a nearly symmetrical pattern of climatic zones north and south of the Equator.

title: 🌍 2.1 OVERVIEW OF WORLD CLIMATIC REGIONS AND TYPES
notes:
🌦️ Global climate → description of Earth's climate as a whole, including regional differences.

☀️ Climate is controlled by energy from the Sun and influenced by temperature, precipitation, latitude, altitude, air pressure, winds, mountains and oceans.

⭐ Climate classification → a system used to group places according to their common climatic conditions.

📌 Climate classification helps to understand expected conditions and supports decisions about :-
🏠 Building materials
🌾 Crop selection
👕 Clothing
🧳 Tourism and travel

🌍 Climate zones generally extend in an east-west direction and may be interrupted by mountains or oceans.

title: 🏛️ 2.1.1 CLIMATE CLASSIFICATIONS
notes:
🏛️ Ancient Greek classification → divided each hemisphere into three zones :-
1️⃣ Torrid (Tropical)
2️⃣ Temperate
3️⃣ Frigid

📊 Modern classifications use long-term records of temperature and precipitation to identify climate patterns.

🌍 Common broad climate types include tropical, dry, temperate, continental and polar climates.

⭐ Wladimir Köppen → German climatologist and botanist who developed one of the most widely used climate classification systems.

📌 Köppen classification uses mean monthly and annual temperature and precipitation.

🔤 Köppen's principal groups :-
A → Humid tropical
B → Dry
C → Humid middle-latitude with mild winters
D → Humid middle-latitude with severe winters
E → Polar
H → Highland

🌡️ A, C, D and E → mainly defined by temperature.
🌧️ B → mainly defined by precipitation.
🏔️ H → determined by altitude.

title: 🌎 2.1.2 WORLD CLIMATE ZONES AND REGIONS
notes:
🌍 Four major global climate zones :-

1️⃣ Tropical Zone → 0°–23.5°
☀️ Receives nearly vertical solar radiation.
🌡️ Very warm throughout the year.
💧 High evaporation and moisture.

2️⃣ Subtropical Zone → 23.5°–40°
☀️ High summer radiation and relatively low moisture.
🏜️ Many of the world's deserts occur here.
❄️ Winters can be relatively cool and moist.

3️⃣ Temperate Zone → 40°–60°
🌡️ Cooler temperatures than the subtropics.
🍂 Strong seasonal differences.
🌧️ Precipitation is generally more regularly distributed.
🌱 Longer vegetation period.

4️⃣ Cold Zone → 60°–90°
❄️ Receives less solar heat because of the low angle of the Sun.
🌗 Large seasonal differences in daylight.
🌱 Vegetation is generally sparse and limited to short periods.

🏔️ Altitude can modify climate within a small area because temperature decreases rapidly with increasing elevation.

title: 🌍 2.2 CLIMATE TYPES AND ZONES OF AFRICA
notes:
🌍 Africa's position across the Equator and the two tropics produces diverse climate conditions.

☀️ Africa lies mainly within the tropical zone and is generally warm and hot.

🌧️ Rainfall varies considerably from one region to another, while temperatures remain generally high.

🏜️ Northern Africa is especially characterized by aridity and high temperatures.

🌊 Mediterranean climate occurs mainly at the northern and southern fringes of the continent.

⭐ Africa has eight major climatic regions :-
1️⃣ Equatorial / Tropical Wet
2️⃣ Tropical Wet-and-Dry
3️⃣ Semi-arid
4️⃣ Hot Desert
5️⃣ Humid Subtropical
6️⃣ Mediterranean
7️⃣ Warm Temperate East Coast
8️⃣ Warm Temperate Continental
9️⃣ Mountain Climate

📌 The textbook also emphasizes the nearly symmetrical distribution of major climate zones north and south of the Equator.

title: 🌧️ 2.2.1.1 EQUATORIAL CLIMATE REGION
notes:
📍 Location → mainly between about 5°N and 5°S of the Equator.

🌍 Main areas → parts of Central Africa including DRC, Gabon and Cameroon; also parts of southern Nigeria, Ghana, Benin and Sierra Leone.

🌡️ Temperature → very high throughout the year, averaging about 26°C.

📊 Diurnal temperature range → very low, about 3°C.

☁️ Heavy cloud cover and high humidity occur throughout the year.

🌧️ Main rainfall type → convectional rainfall.

🌿 Equatorial areas are among the wettest parts of Africa.

🏔️ Highland and coastal areas, especially in East Africa, may experience modified equatorial conditions with lower temperatures.

title: 🌾 2.2.1.2 TROPICAL WET-AND-DRY REGION
notes:
🌿 Also called → Savanna climatic region, although not every savanna vegetation area has this climate.

📍 Distribution → covers a little less than half of Africa and extends toward the Equator from semiarid regions.

🌧️ Main characteristic → strongly seasonal rainfall.

☀️ During the high-sun period → maritime air masses bring rainfall, sometimes for up to six months.

☀️ During the rest of the year → conditions are mainly dry.

🌬️ Harmattan → warm, dry northeasterly/easterly wind blowing from the southern Sahara over West Africa, often carrying sand and dust.

🌧️ Equatorial areas may experience two rainfall peaks because of the double passage of the ITCZ.

title: 🏜️ 2.2.1.3 SEMI-ARID CLIMATIC REGION
notes:
🏜️ Semi-arid climate → climate found around desert margins with more rainfall than true deserts.

📍 Distribution → fringes desert areas and includes much of the land south of the Zambezi River.

🌧️ Rainfall → greater than in true desert regions because the area comes within the seasonal influence of the ITCZ.

🌡️ Temperature → generally similar to desert regions.

⚠️ Semi-arid areas are vulnerable to drought and desertification when rainfall becomes insufficient or variable.

title: 🏜️ 2.2.1.4 HOT DESERT CLIMATIC REGION
notes:
🏜️ Hot desert climate → areas receiving little or no rainfall.

📍 Major African examples → Sahara, Kalahari and northern Kenya–Somali desert.

🌡️ Daytime temperatures → commonly about 30°C–40°C and may exceed 40°C.

🌙 Night temperatures → may fall below 10°C.

📊 Diurnal temperature range → greater than the annual range of mean monthly temperature.

☀️ Skies are generally clear, allowing rapid heat loss at night.

📌 The Sahara is influenced by dry continental tropical air masses.

🌊 The northern Kenya–Somali desert is strongly associated with stable maritime air masses passing over cool offshore waters.

title: 🌴 2.2.1.5 HUMID SUBTROPICAL CLIMATIC REGION
notes:
📍 General location → eastern sides of continents between about 20° and 35° north and south.

🇿🇦 In Africa → mainly confined to the southeastern coast of South Africa.

🌡️ Climate → relatively warm and wet.

🌍 Transitional nature → lies between tropical and temperate climates.

🔤 Köppen classification → includes Cfa and Cwa climates.

title: 🌊 2.2.1.6 MEDITERRANEAN CLIMATE REGION
notes:
🌍 Mediterranean climate → also called Warm Temperate Western Margin Climate.

📍 Africa → mainly around the Mediterranean coast of North Africa and the southwestern tip of the continent.

🌡️ Temperature → about 10°C in winter to about 21°C in summer.

☀️ Summer → generally dry because winds blow from land toward the sea.

🌧️ Winter → wet because cool, moist westerly winds move from sea toward land.

🌧️ Average annual rainfall → about 500–750 mm.

🌤️ Clear and blue skies are common.

⭐ Key feature → dry summers and mild, wet winters.

title: 🌊 2.2.1.7 WARM TEMPERATE EAST COAST CLIMATE
notes:
📍 Location → eastern coast of South Africa, especially Natal and Cape Provinces, and parts of Mozambique.

🧭 Latitude → approximately 30°–40° north and south in the general global zone described.

🌊 Main controls → warm Mozambique Current and warm southeast trade winds.

🌡️ Summer → generally high, averaging about 26°C.

❄️ Winter → averages about 10°C.

🌧️ Annual rainfall → about 1,000–1,500 mm.

📉 Rainfall decreases westward toward the interior.

title: 🌾 2.2.1.8 WARM TEMPERATE CONTINENTAL CLIMATE
notes:
📍 Location → interior of South Africa, between the Drakensberg Mountains and Kalahari Desert.

🌧️ Rainfall → generally low because the region is inland and moisture-bearing winds lose much of their moisture before reaching it.

🌧️ Most rainfall → occurs during winter.

📊 Average annual rainfall → about 700 mm.

🧭 Eastern areas → wetter than western areas near the Kalahari Desert.

🌡️ Temperature → about 26°C in summer and about 10°C in winter.

title: 🏔️ 2.2.1.9 MOUNTAIN CLIMATIC REGION
notes:
🏔️ Location → high mountain areas of Kenya, Ethiopia and the East African lakes region.

🌡️ Temperature → decreases with increasing altitude.

❄️ Highest peaks → may have snow, such as Mount Kilimanjaro.

🌧️ Rainfall → generally greater than surrounding areas.

⛰️ Relief rainfall → warm moist air is forced to rise over highlands.

🌧️ Windward slopes → receive the greatest rainfall.

🏜️ Leeward/rain-shadow slopes → receive little or no rainfall because descending air is drier.

📌 Lapse rate → average temperature decrease of about 6.4°C for every 1,000 m increase in altitude.

❄️ Very high mountain tops may have temperatures below freezing.

title: 🌍 2.2.2 FACTORS CONTROLLING CLIMATE OF AFRICA
notes:
⭐ Major climate controls of Africa :-

1️⃣ Angle of the Sun
2️⃣ Latitude
3️⃣ Air pressure
4️⃣ Wind systems
5️⃣ Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
6️⃣ Major ocean currents
7️⃣ Distribution of land and water
8️⃣ Altitude

🌡️ These factors mainly determine temperature and precipitation.

☀️ Latitude → affects the amount and angle of solar radiation received.

🌬️ Air pressure and winds → control movement of air masses and rainfall.

🌍 ITCZ → controls seasonal movement of rainfall.

🌊 Ocean currents → modify temperature and moisture along coastal areas.

🌊 Land and water → create differences between continental and maritime climates.

🏔️ Altitude → temperature decreases as elevation increases.

title: ☀️ LATITUDE AND SOLAR RADIATION
notes:
🌍 Africa extends approximately from 37°N to 34°S and straddles the Equator.

☀️ The Equator receives relatively direct solar radiation, producing high temperatures.

📉 As latitude increases, sunlight reaches the surface more obliquely and provides less energy.

🌡️ Therefore, latitude produces differences in solar energy and temperature across Africa.

⭐ Africa's location largely explains why warm and tropical climates dominate the continent.

title: 🌬️ PRESSURE SYSTEMS, WINDS AND ITCZ
notes:
🌍 Subtropical high-pressure belts → located around 30° north and south and help control wind patterns, rainfall and temperature.

🌬️ Northeast Trade Winds → blow from the northern subtropical high-pressure belt toward the ITCZ.

🏜️ Harmattan → dry and cool northeast/east wind affecting Sub-Saharan Africa, approximately November–April.

🌧️ Southwest Trade Winds / Monsoon → moist winds from the southern subtropical high-pressure belt that bring rainfall to parts of West Africa.

🌍 ITCZ → zone where major trade winds converge near the Equator.

🔄 ITCZ moves north and south with the seasonal movement of the Sun.

☀️ June → ITCZ reaches about 13°N near the southern boundary of the Sahara.

❄️ December → ITCZ moves southward along the West African coast toward the Congo Basin and Madagascar.

🌧️ ITCZ movement is closely associated with the distribution and seasonal pattern of rainfall in Africa.

title: 🌊 MAJOR OCEAN CURRENTS AND AFRICAN CLIMATE
notes:
🌊 Ocean current → movement of ocean water that influences the temperature and moisture characteristics of winds and nearby coastal areas.

🔥 Warm ocean currents → carry warm water toward cooler regions and supply moisture to winds, encouraging rainfall.

🌊 Warm Guinea Current → affects West Africa.
🌊 Warm Mozambique Current → affects Southeast Africa.

❄️ Cool ocean currents → cool the air above them, encourage moisture condensation and often produce dry coastal conditions.

❄️ Cool Canary Current → affects the western coast of the Sahara.
❄️ Cool Benguela Current → affects the western coast near the Kalahari/Namib region.

🎣 Cool currents can create rich fishing grounds.
📍 Rich fishing grounds occur along the Morocco and Spanish Saharan coasts influenced by the Canary Current and along the Namibian coast influenced by the Benguela Current.

title: 🌊 LAND, WATER AND CONTINENTALITY
notes:
🌊 Large water bodies → moderate the climate of nearby land.

🏜️ Continental interiors → experience greater temperature extremes because land heats and cools more rapidly than water.

☀️ Daytime/summer → land heats rapidly.
🌙 Night/winter → land loses heat rapidly.

🌧️ Interior areas may receive less rainfall because moisture-bearing winds lose moisture before reaching them.

🏙️ Continental climate → climate of inland areas with greater temperature ranges.

🌊 Maritime climate → climate of areas influenced strongly by nearby oceans or large water bodies.

📍 Example → Timbuktu in Mali has high diurnal and annual temperature ranges because of continentality.

title: 🏔️ ALTITUDE AND CLIMATE
notes:
🏔️ Altitude → height of a place above sea level.

🌡️ Temperature decreases as altitude increases.

📉 Lapse rate → average temperature decrease of about 6.4°C per 1,000 m.

🇪🇹 Ethiopian Highlands → have relatively cool temperatures because of high elevation.

🏔️ Mount Kilimanjaro → despite being near the Equator, its high elevation allows permanent snow cover.

⭐ Altitude can create major climatic differences within relatively short horizontal distances.

title: 🌍 2.3 BENEFITS OF CLIMATE FOR LIFE OF PEOPLE IN AFRICA
notes:
🌦️ Climate affects almost every aspect of human life.

⭐ It influences :-
🌾 Food production
🏘️ Settlement patterns
💼 Livelihoods
🏥 Health and wellbeing
🚢 Transport infrastructure
👕 Clothing
🏖️ Recreation and tourism
🌿 Natural resources
💧 Water availability

🏘️ Areas with favorable climatic conditions often support greater population concentrations.

🏜️ Areas with extreme conditions, such as deserts and other harsh environments, generally have fewer people.

🌍 Africa's climatic diversity, from intense heat to very cold highland conditions, produces different lifestyles and livelihood opportunities.

title: 🌾 2.3.1 CLIMATE AND AGRICULTURE IN AFRICA
notes:
🌾 Agriculture → a major livelihood and economic activity across Africa.

☀️🌧️ Successful crop production depends strongly on suitable combinations of sunlight, warmth and rainfall.

🌧️ Much of Sub-Saharan Africa → highly dependent on rain-fed agriculture and natural resources.

📊 Agriculture is described in the textbook as accounting on average for about 70% of Africa's labor force and more than 25% of GDP.

⚠️ Climate variability can strongly affect agricultural production because many farmers depend on seasonal rainfall.

👨‍🌾 Small-scale and subsistence farmers are particularly vulnerable when technology, finance and infrastructure are limited.

title: 🏥 2.3.2 CLIMATE AND HEALTH IN AFRICA
notes:
🏥 Climate affects human health through environmental and social conditions.

🌊 Floods → can cause drowning and other health problems.

🏜️ Drought → can cause crop failure, food shortages and hunger.

🌡️ Temperature extremes → increase risks from excessive heat or cold.

🦠 Climate conditions can also influence disease outbreaks through complex environmental and human processes.

⚠️ Africa is highly climate-vulnerable because rainfall variability, hydrological extremes and climate change can affect large populations.

title: 💧 2.3.3 CLIMATE AND WATER RESOURCES IN AFRICA
notes:
💧 Water → one of the most important natural resources for life.

🌧️ Climate influences the amount and availability of water.

🌊 Climate affects :-
• Stream and river levels
• River flow
• Underground water
• Surface-water supply

⚠️ Persistent climate change may reduce surface-water supplies and affect the quantity and regularity of rivers and streams.

⭐ Water availability therefore connects climate directly with livelihoods, agriculture, health and development.

title: 🌡️ 2.4 CLIMATE CHANGE AND AFRICA'S DEVELOPMENT VISION
notes:
🌍 Climate variability → variation in climate conditions that may result from natural internal processes or external human-related forcing.

🌡️ Climate change → a persistent change in the average state or variability of the climate system, generally lasting decades or longer.

⚠️ Africa is among the continents most vulnerable to climate change.

📌 Major reasons for vulnerability :-
1️⃣ Weak adaptive capacity
2️⃣ Strong dependence on ecosystem resources
3️⃣ Less-developed agricultural production systems
4️⃣ High dependence on rainfall for food production

⭐ Climate change threatens agriculture, food security, water resources, ecosystems, health and sustainable development.

title: ⚠️ MAJOR IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE IN AFRICA
notes:
🌡️ Higher temperatures
🌊 Rising sea levels
🌧️ Changing rainfall patterns
🔄 Increased climate variability
🌾 Reduced agricultural production
🍽️ Threats to food security
🏜️ Drying soils and desertification
🦠 Increased pests and diseases
🌱 Changes in suitable areas for crops and livestock
🌊 Flooding
🌳 Deforestation
🌍 Soil erosion
💧 Pressure on water supply
🏥 Health problems
🏛️ Pressure on political stability

⭐ Climate change is therefore an environmental, social and economic threat to Africa.

title: 🌍 CLIMATE CHANGE AND AFRICA'S DEVELOPMENT
notes:
📈 Climate change can make development more difficult by increasing pressure on agriculture, water, health and political stability.

🎯 It can affect Africa's ability to achieve development objectives, including the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) and Africa's 2063 development goal.

⚠️ Africa's vulnerability is increased because many people depend directly on rainfall and natural resources for their livelihoods.

🌍 The continent also faces complex climate systems and potentially large changes in rainfall and temperature.

🛡️ Low adaptive capacity makes climate impacts more difficult to manage.

⭐ Sustainable development therefore requires greater ability to adapt to changing climatic conditions.

title: 🧠 UNIT 2 KEY TERMS
notes:
🌦️ Climate → average weather conditions over a long period, usually 30 years or more.

☁️ Weather → short-term atmospheric condition.

🌍 Climate zone → broad area with similar climatic conditions.

📍 Climate region → continuous geographic area with similar climate characteristics.

📊 Climate classification → system for grouping climates according to common characteristics.

🌡️ Köppen classification → widely used system based mainly on temperature and precipitation.

🌍 ITCZ → zone where major trade winds converge and which shifts seasonally with the Sun.

🌬️ Harmattan → dry, cool northeast/east wind affecting Sub-Saharan Africa.

🌊 Ocean current → movement of ocean water that influences nearby climate.

🏜️ Continental climate → inland climate with relatively large temperature ranges.

🌊 Maritime climate → climate strongly influenced by nearby water bodies.

🏔️ Altitude → height above sea level.

📉 Lapse rate → decrease in temperature with increasing altitude, about 6.4°C per 1,000 m in the textbook.

🌧️ Relief rainfall → rainfall produced when moist air rises over highland areas.

🌧️ Windward slope → side of a mountain facing moisture-bearing winds and usually receiving more rainfall.

🏜️ Leeward/rain-shadow slope → side away from moisture-bearing winds and generally receiving less rainfall.

🔄 Climate variability → variation in climate conditions over time.

🌡️ Climate change → long-term persistent change in climate conditions or their variability.

title: ⭐ UNIT 2 QUICK REVISION
notes:
📌 Climate → average weather conditions over 30 years or more.

📌 Weather → short-term atmospheric condition.

📌 Ancient Greek climate classification → Torrid, Temperate and Frigid.

📌 Köppen classification → A, B, C, D, E and H groups.

📌 Four major global climate zones → Tropical, Subtropical, Temperate and Cold.

📌 Africa is mainly located within the tropics and is generally warm and hot.

📌 Africa has a nearly symmetrical pattern of major climate zones north and south of the Equator.

📌 Major African climatic regions → Equatorial, Tropical Wet-and-Dry, Semi-arid, Hot Desert, Humid Subtropical, Mediterranean, Warm Temperate East Coast, Warm Temperate Continental and Mountain.

📌 Equatorial climate → very hot, humid and wet; mainly receives convectional rainfall.

📌 Tropical wet-and-dry climate → seasonal rainfall with a distinct dry period.

📌 Semi-arid climate → transitional climate around deserts with more rainfall than true deserts.

📌 Hot desert climate → very little rainfall, high daytime temperatures and large daily temperature ranges.

📌 Mediterranean climate → dry summers and wet winters.

📌 Warm temperate east coast climate → influenced strongly by the warm Mozambique Current and southeast trade winds.

📌 Warm temperate continental climate → mainly interior South Africa with relatively low rainfall.

📌 Mountain climate → controlled strongly by altitude and relief; windward slopes are wetter than leeward slopes.

📌 Major climate controls → Sun angle, latitude, pressure systems, winds, ITCZ, ocean currents, land-water distribution and altitude.

📌 Warm ocean currents → generally add moisture and can increase coastal rainfall.

📌 Cool ocean currents → generally produce drier coastal conditions and may create rich fishing grounds.

📌 ITCZ → seasonal movement strongly controls rainfall distribution.

📌 Altitude → temperature decreases about 6.4°C per 1,000 m.

📌 Climate influences agriculture, settlement, livelihoods, health, water resources, transport, clothing and tourism.

📌 Climate change threatens agriculture, food security, water resources, ecosystems, health and development.

📌 Major climate-change impacts → higher temperatures, sea-level rise, changing rainfall, drought, floods, desertification, pests, diseases, deforestation and erosion.

⭐ Core idea → Africa's climate is controlled by its tropical location, atmospheric circulation, ocean currents, land-water distribution and altitude; climate strongly shapes human life and development, while climate change creates major environmental, social and economic challenges.
